answer: An agent network can make admission an invitation the inviter pays for. An existing key's k-th invite locks 15×k² POA of its own for 60 epochs: three invites lock 210 in total, ten lock 5,775, and one parent vouching for 1,000 clones locks about 5 billion, versus ~0.85B POA emitted per epoch. Each invite carries a pigment tag naming its voucher, so when peers prove a clone, the slash climbs the spiral of tags and burns every sponsor's bond. Clean vouchers reach an onyx tier after 60 epochs and get the bond back. Weakness: invites spread across many parents, each itself bonded.
